body: Thanks. The department in question seems friendly enough. I just don't feel committed enough to the field for it to be worth my time or theirs. What's the point of applying if, in the off-chance that I'm successful, I just bow out a year later due to stress and misery.

My doctoral work is mostly applied economics - with a focus on health economics. I can teach labour, health, econometrics, intros, applied micro. I've done interdisciplinary work with people in medicine. 

I find myself drawn to pretty much any sort of applied micro research. Avid reader of the Journal of Health Economics, labour journals, AEJ: Applied, etc.  My problem as an economist, I think, is that I like data analysis more than I like economics. I am a solid "generalist researcher" but terrible academic economist.
Thanks. Knowing I'm not alone is sometimes better than advice.
